what_went_wrong: Will not conclude that the 'exclusively managed' charter clause is a general s141(a) recitation that leaves the veto enforceable under s122(18); calls enforceability 'materially uncertain'
rationale: The memo states the synopsis rule correctly, then says Avalon's clause 'goes further than the statutory default' and that Avalon 'should not assume' the amendment overrides 'exclusively'. The expert applies the synopsis and commits. Mode C: the rule is stated but not applied; secondary K because the memo treats the rubric's reading as the 'counterargument'. Material: core answer to question 1. The model opened the SB 313 page, so no longer harness-aggravated; D2. Softer than the first run, which asserted unenforceability.

what_went_wrong: Invented revenue bases, cash margins, timing and a 10-year horizon, then reported point NPVs and IRRs, despite 'directional estimates, not exact calculations'
rationale: The reference gives only capex, growth rates and a 30% failure chance. The model added Year 1 revenue of $25m, 20% and 25% cash conversion and a two-year delay for B, and reports 'About +$8m' against 'About +$25m' NPV and 12% against 16% IRR; the headline that B's value is 'roughly three times A's' rests on them. The expert's report stays directional. Mode I, an explicit instruction broken; secondary C, too precise for the evidence. Send back; D2.

what_went_wrong: Regional comparison shows only the four named dollar metrics: no EBITDA %, SG&A % or GM %, no direct costs and no percentage view
basis: fresh (decision rule 3; same kind of gap as F-B4)
rationale: The task wants regions compared for senior management, and Region A's revenue is about 20 times Region F's, so ratios are needed for a fair comparison. The tab has Revenue, SG&A, Allocations and EBITDA in dollars only; EBITDA cannot even be traced without COGS. F-B4 ruled the same omission real for Opus, which at least showed EBITDA %. Mode P, minor, D1; no expert file, so it rests on the task wording and that precedent.

what_went_wrong: Electric bass classed as an 'electronic instrument': the bass player gets a 25% all-work premium ($590.86) on top of the chair premium and doubling
rationale: CBA 4.2(f)(i) is about synthesizers and samplers 'regardless of the type of controller', and 4.2(c) lists electric bass as an ordinary instrument; the expert and Opus both give the bass 15% plus doubling only. The model also left both guitars as non-electronic, so the treatment is inconsistent. Mode K: a contract term is misapplied; secondary C, a precise figure built on a self-declared assumption. Send back rather than material because the workbook flags the classification for verification and marks the sample as not approved; D1.

what_went_wrong: Standards of review explained more thinly than the expert's: never says entire fairness is the most demanding standard, or that business-judgment deference gives way to fraud or waste
rationale: The client is not a lawyer and asked how a court would review the deal. The memo says only that entire fairness is 'the starting point' and that courts 'do not second-guess an ordinary business decision'. The expert's memo has both statements almost word for word (decision rule 4). Mode P, minor, D1; the memo is 2,162 words against a 3,500 limit, so length did not force the omission.

what_went_wrong: SAR narrative has no per-account summary by transaction category with count, minimum, maximum and total
rationale: The narrative gives count and total of cash deposits per account and some category totals for accounts 6 and 7, but no minimum or maximum amounts and no category breakdown for accounts 1 to 5; the Excel has none either. The expert's SAR has the full breakdown for all seven accounts, so decision rule 4 makes this a real failure. Mode P: an omission with no wrong fact and no broken instruction. Minor: the totals a reader needs are present; D1: worked SAR narratives would teach the format.

what_went_wrong: Summary of the 2019 FTC case leaves out that the data was used for targeted advertising and that parents' class actions followed
rationale: The task asked for a summary of relevant case law. The memo gives the settlement and cites Jones v. Google but never says the complaint alleged use for targeted advertising, or that Jones was a follow-up class action by parents. The expert's memo states both (decision rule 4). Mode P, minor, D1.

what_went_wrong: Never says s122(18) was enacted in response to Moelis
rationale: The memo places Moelis 'before the 2024 amendment' and calls the opinion 'the historical problem', but never states the causal link. The expert does. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: 'Injunction' used twice with no plain-language explanation
rationale: The task required plain language for a client, and the memo says 'Relief is generally an injunction and restitution' without explaining either word. That breaks an explicit instruction, so the mode is I. Minor: a reviewer would note it and not block. D1: expert client memos show the register.

what_went_wrong: Capitalization representation omits that prior issuances violated no pre-emptive or similar rights
rationale: Section 3.2 says outstanding shares were validly issued 'in compliance with applicable securities laws' and that the new shares are free of pre-emptive rights, but gives no representation about prior issuances. The task asked for customary representations and the expert's agreement has this one (decision rule 4). Mode P; minor, since the founder has always held every share. D1.

what_went_wrong: Personal-effects list or letter declared 'advisory only'; no request that it be honored
rationale: Section 3.4 says a list or letter 'is advisory only' and never asks the executor to honor it. That is a softened commitment (grading rule 2); a non-binding request to honor would have fitted the sole-discretion instruction. Mode C. I rate it minor, because the statement is legally accurate and a reviewer would not block on it. D2.

what_went_wrong: No executor power over digital accounts, assets and devices
rationale: The will has no digital-asset clause; a search for digital, electronic, online, device, email and password finds nothing. The task asked for customary clauses and standard fiduciary powers, and this is substance a Texas will normally carries (decision rule 3). Mode P, minor, D1. There is no expert file, so this rests on judgement.

what_went_wrong: No driver age distribution, although the model searched the Korea Transportation Safety Authority's site
basis: fresh (first-run S-F-10 was E4; web search was available this time)
rationale: No slide gives driver ages. Raw responses show 25 completed web-search actions including 'site.kotsa.or.kr' queries and one with '65세', with no error status; the deck says only that restricted TIMS microdata 'were not obtained'. The nationwide taxi count, missing in the first run, is now present (230,458). Mode P; minor; D3.

what_went_wrong: No fee or commission comparison with a competitor
basis: fresh (first-run S-F-10 was E4; web search was available this time)
rationale: Appendix A2 models an assumed 'effective net revenue yield' of 0-6% and cites no fee for SuperK-T, its public analogue or Kakao. None of the 17 search actions asks about fees or commissions, so the model did not look. Mode P; minor; D3.

what_went_wrong: Payment localisation is generic: 'local-card and wallet pilot' with no named Korean payment or ecosystem partner
rationale: Slide 3 names no Korean wallet, card scheme, map or super-app. The task makes Korean user experience a key hurdle and asks for a localized, actionable plan, so a named integration is substance a professional would include (decision rule 3). Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Rubric and expert wage rates are above the contract excerpt; the model used the contract's rates
expert_meets_item: yes (the rubric figures are the expert's, at the expert's rates)
rationale: The CBA excerpt gives $251.06, $2,008.50, $55.67 and $76.59; the expert's Rates sheet and the rubric use 252.06, 2,016.48, 56.67 and 77.59. The model's Rates row holds the contract figures, and all 23 values equal the expert's method recomputed at contract rates to within 1 cent. The ruling is about the rubric, so it carries over, and the model's file was checked against it.

what_went_wrong: Doubling pay computed on scale wages only, not compounded on the chair premium (the contract gives no base)
rationale: CBA 4.4 says only '25% additional pay' and names no base. The model applies the right tiers (25%, 35%, 45%) to base wages and states 'No compounding' in its Guide with a note to verify; the expert applies doubling to wages plus premium. Both readings fit the text. Covers doubling for bass, Guitar A, trumpet and woodwind, and the vacation and total lines for Guitar A, trumpet and woodwind.

what_went_wrong: Rubric enforces the expert's EOR/MIR IDs, two named tabs and a Testing Type column against the task's SCRA-12a to SCRA-18 IDs
rationale: The new file uses exactly the task's ten IDs (Test Questions A9:A18) on one sheet, with s3937 citations on 12a-d and s3919 citations on 13-18. The rubric contradicts the task (decision rule 3).

what_went_wrong: No 2 CFR citation on topics 1-5 and 11; the task asks for citations on topics 6-10 only
rationale: The task scopes Uniform Guidance references to topics 6 to 10, and the model cited exactly those five. The rubric follows the expert's file, which cites all 11. Sections 200.206 and 200.208 appear only in the Purpose line, not in question 11, so the high-risk item is not met as written.

what_went_wrong: Rubric's Schedule A line 5a ($2,246) is the state table amount only; the model added the local sales tax the IRS worksheet requires ($719), so lines 5a, 12, 15, 16, 24 and 37 differ
rationale: Same figures as Opus on all six lines (2,965; 31,692; 329,211; 62,280; 57,973; 14,781) and the same method: IRS table amount $2,246 plus the 2.00/6.25 local ratio, with the jurisdiction flagged for confirmation. The expert's Schedule A omits the local step. Same reading as O2-A-1.

what_went_wrong: Source's single 'Other Costs' block split between Other Tour and Other Travel differently from the rubric
rationale: The source has one 'Other Costs' block per tab and the task gives no mapping. The model put jet, transfer cars and car service in Travel and commission, insurance, other, petty cash and fees in Tour, and disclosed this on three tabs. Total expenses (732,005.50) and net income (120,422.94) match the rubric. It is the same split and reasoning as A-R3, decided fresh from this file.

what_went_wrong: Reported the final trial balance as supplied and flagged the $49,137.41 prepaid-insurance difference; the expert booked it
rationale: The model's TB tab reproduces the supplied final TB (net 497,479.81; assets 33,955,902.02). The rubric's figures are exactly 49,137.41 lower because the expert posted the insurance write-off into the TB. The task says to flag inconsistencies and notify the CFO before finalizing, and the model raised it as high-priority issue I03 with the amount and accounts. Same reasoning as A-R6, decided fresh.

what_went_wrong: Substitute-synthesizer clause read differently from the expert: 150% of base for the show, plus 25% electronic premium on rehearsal, sound check and both audits
rationale: CBA 4.2(f)(ii) is ambiguous ('the lesser of 150% of the base wage for each show ... or the weekly guaranteed wage and a 25% premium'). The model takes the literal 'lesser of' reading and discloses it in its Guide; the expert pays a 50% premium on show, rehearsal and sound check. The model's premium is $339.80 against $303.00 for the expert's method at contract rates. The 25% premium on audits is the weakest part (see Doubts).

what_went_wrong: Rubric expects a phantom $1 of Additional Medicare Tax withholding (Form 8959 lines 19 and 24, Form 1040 line 25c)
expert_meets_item: n/a (expert is the source of the $1)
rationale: The model shows 5,124, 0 and 0, the correct amounts from adding the cents and rounding the total. The rubric's figures come from the expert's per-W-2 rounding.

what_went_wrong: No conclusion that Marcus likely breached: 'substantial but fact- and characterization-dependent controller exposure, with meaningful contractual and status-quo defenses'
basis: my decision 2026-11-11 (second-run dispute 2); cold check S03
rationale: Not met as written: the memo gives no bottom line. The hedge rests on Sears, the case the task linked, which lets a controller use his own rights to keep things as they are; a veto does that. All three memos raise this defence and the expert's memo does not. Opus's bottom line on the same point is 'a substantial risk' and was passed by a different judge. A hedge is a failure when the source settles the point and defensible when the source leaves it open. Moved out of S2-L-2, which is left with no items.

what_went_wrong: Regions A-G do not sum to All Company for SG&A, Allocations and EBITDA because Corporate is kept as a separate bridge row
rationale: The source file records Corporate outside Regions A-G and puts every allocation dollar in Corporate. The model shows Branch subtotal + Corporate = All Company with a zero bridge check and discloses that it did not spread Corporate costs. Revenue ties exactly. It is a disclosed allocation judgement.

what_went_wrong: Rubric requires benefits-eligibility and tax-eligibility mapping tables that the Assumptions do not contain
expert_meets_item: no (the expert's file has neither table)
rationale: The reference Assumptions define five pay types and one payroll tax with three bands; there are no benefits and no exclusions by pay type. The model applies the three bands to all five pay types per employee, with the caps enforced. The rubric asks for content that cannot be produced from the inputs.

what_went_wrong: No roadmap sentence, no 'how do you wish to proceed' line, no statement of support, no sign-off
rationale: These four are letter conventions taken from the expert's memo; the task asked for none of them (decision rule 3, style). The memo opens with a 'Bottom line' paragraph that does the roadmap's job and closes with a Recommendation paragraph. It uses a To/From memo format, which has no sign-off.

what_went_wrong: States the Sears duty not to harm 'through gross negligence' but never applies it to Marcus; notes 'statutory controller protection against monetary care liability'
rationale: Same reading as O2-L-1 and H2-L-5. This memo's disclosure is the thinnest of the three: one sentence, and it conditions the protection on the statutory transaction category. Close call; see Doubts.

what_went_wrong: Neither memo states that Avalon is a Delaware corporation
rationale: The memo says it 'addresses Delaware corporate law' and applies it throughout, but has no sentence that Avalon is a Delaware corporation, in the .docx or the .pdf. The expert's memo has none either.

what_went_wrong: Rubric wants a Corporate Banking / Marine Finance / Brazil sample; the task says 'CB Trade Finance Brazil' and the Population has no Trade Finance
rationale: The rubric maps the task's 'Trade Finance' to 'Marine Finance', a mapping found in neither the task nor the Population file. The model documented the entity as unavailable, declined to invent a mapping and sampled a Corporate Bank Brazil row (No 138, Fund Services) as a supplement. This is the rubric naming a different business from the task (decision rule 3).

what_went_wrong: AP Trade items need AP_TB-1.xlsx, which the dataset does not include; the model flagged it as missing
rationale: The task names AP_TB-1.xlsx but it is not among the 17 reference files and no copy exists under data/. The model marked the tab MISSING SOURCE and made it issue I01. The expert had the file, so 313,891.43 and 672.35 cannot be produced from the supplied inputs.

what_went_wrong: The added 'March TB reference' tab carries no April 2025 period; the expert's file has no period on four tabs
rationale: The item is read as at Opus table review 3: it is met if each tab from 3a onward states the April 2025 period. Every tab does except the added March reference tab 20, which holds March data and no April period. The expert's file has no period text on 3a, 10, 11a and 11b, so the expert does not meet the item either (decision rule 4).

what_went_wrong: SAR states the amount involved as $1,980,075.22 (cash deposits only), not the rubric's $4,559,667 (every credit plus every debit)
rationale: The model's figure is computed correctly and disclosed with a reason (avoid double counting), and the SAR also gives total credits and total debits, which sum to the rubric's figure. The rubric's figure counts every transaction in both directions, including ride-share purchases and card settlements, which is disputable. The task's three red flags are all cash-based. This is the closest call in the list.

what_went_wrong: A rehearsal under 3 hours is paid at the 3-hour minimum call instead of flagged; over 5 consecutive hours is flagged
expert_meets_item: partly (flags each rehearsal row under 3h or over 5h, not per-day totals)
rationale: The rubric's per-day totals are not in the contract: 7.1 is a minimum call and 7.5 limits consecutive hours without a meal break. The model pays MAX(3, hours), flags more than 5 consecutive hours and checks for sub-30-minute gaps. That applies the contract's actual rules, as Opus did.

what_went_wrong: Order growth measured on Orders (Units), not the dollar Orders account
rationale: The task says 'YoY percent order growth' without naming units or dollars. The model uses units and says so in the Guide. Recomputed from the raw file, the ranking of the 10 branches is identical on either basis.

what_went_wrong: Conclusion recommends a committee 'potentially supplemented by a minority vote', not both MFW protections from the outset
basis: fresh (expert-file fact from table review 4, re-read)
rationale: The item is not met: the second protection is optional (grading rule 2). The expert's Conclusion recommends 'at least one (if not both)' safeguards, so it fails the item too. Under amended § 144(b) one protection suffices for this deal, so this is not an objective error.

what_went_wrong: Top-up applies to Exempt Issuances too; the expert's agreement does the same
rationale: As written the item wants Exempt Issuances excluded from the top-up, and section 7.3 says an Exempt Issuance that would breach the floor still triggers it. The expert's Exempt Issuances clause says those issuances 'shall remain subject to Section 4.3(a)', the minimum-ownership covenant, so the expert's file has the same design. Both also allow a par-value payment only where law requires it.

what_went_wrong: 21-year trust cap measured from the testator's death, with the conflict flagged for client approval
rationale: The will follows the task's 'maximum trust duration of 21 years' literally and makes it control over the age-25 rule. A cover note explains the conflict and asks the supervising attorney to get client approval. The rubric's lives-in-being version is not what the task said.

what_went_wrong: s3937 questions refer to the eligibility and notice conditions through a defined term and a statutory cross-reference; the conditions are written out on the Instructions sheet, not in a question
rationale: SCRA-12b says 'the covered mortgage' and SCRA-12a says 's3937(b)'s notice-and-proof requirements'; pre-service incurrence (Instructions B6) and written notice, orders, extension orders and the 180-day deadline (B7) are stated correctly on the Instructions sheet, which the question sheet tells the tester to read first. Both items are not met as written because no question states the conditions. The content is present and correct in the deliverable and only its placement differs from the rubric's, so this is classed as a disclosed design choice. Close call: see Doubts.

what_went_wrong: Rubric's legal balance (870,569.38) copies a double count in Legal_Dump-1.xlsx; the model used the GL figure 435,284.69
rationale: In the source, L62 = SUM(L3:L61) re-adds the L60 subtotal, doubling the account. The supplied TB shows 435,284.69, which the model reports and ties, documenting the fix. The expert's file carries the doubled figure.

what_went_wrong: 'March' strings appear in rows 1 to 10: bonus-accrual source rows, a flag note, a reference tab and the change log
rationale: The April source file AccrBonus-1.xlsx itself has 'March reverse against actual paid' and 'March Accrual' in rows 9 and 10, so any faithful schedule fails the item, and the expert's tab 17 has the same two rows. The model's other hits are a flag the task asked for, the change log and the March filename the task told it to cite. Neither file meets the item.

what_went_wrong: Monthly trend income statement ends at EBIT; no Net Income line
rationale: The raw file has 21 accounts and none is interest or tax, so EBIT is the lowest line the data supports. The model states 'No interest or taxes were provided.'

what_went_wrong: Rubric asks for a From block naming Sullivan Bryson Privacy Advocates LLP; the task names the firm X Privacy Law
expert_meets_item: yes (under the rubric's own firm name)
rationale: The task says the firm is X Privacy Law and the memo's From line says exactly that. The expert's own From line also names only the firm, with no attorney. The rubric was written for a different firm name, so the item cannot be met by following the task.

what_went_wrong: Rubric expects a discussion of arbitration and class-waiver terms written for the rubric's other platform (VueVid)
rationale: The Opus ruling is that the item belongs to the rubric's other platform and YouTube's terms have no arbitration clause. The model asserts nothing wrong: it lists 'any arbitration/class-waiver provisions' as something to verify, without explaining implications. The expert's memo never mentions arbitration either.

what_went_wrong: No FTC press-release link (no internet); the case is identified by parties, amount and docket number
rationale: The model had no internet and could not open or verify a web address. The memo identifies the settlement by parties, $170 million, court and docket number, as Opus's did. Same harness limit as the Opus ruling.

what_went_wrong: Memo says California law is violated only by sale or sharing without parental opt-in, not by collection alone; rubric wants a summary that CCPA/CPRA may have been violated by the collection
rationale: On content the item is not met: the memo summarises a possible COPPA violation but says California imposes no blanket parental-consent rule for collection. That position is the more accurate one, and the expert's own section II.B states the opt-in rule as a sale-or-sharing rule. The rubric's version is disputable, and the item also carries the VueVid naming mismatch (L-R3).

what_went_wrong: No prevailing-party fee clause; enforcement counsel fees are recovered through the indemnity instead
rationale: Section 11.3 lets a party recover 'reasonable enforcement costs (including reasonable counsel fees)' arising from the other's breach. That gives the client fee recovery by a different mechanism, and one that does not expose him to paying the company's fees if he loses. The task did not ask for a prevailing-party clause. Close call against a minor real failure.

what_went_wrong: No in-app or in-vehicle advertising lever
basis: fresh (same reasoning as S-F-11 and F-K2)
rationale: 'Ads' in the deck are SuperK-T's own customer marketing. The task never mentions advertising; other monetization levers are proposed (corporate accounts, booking APIs, a fee-paying mix).

what_went_wrong: Inbound demand is reached through hotel, eSIM and travel-agency referrals and airport pickup guides, not a partnership with airport taxi companies
rationale: Slide 3 sets a goal of '50 hotel partners' and 'airport pickup guides'; fleet partnerships on slide 2 are not airport-specific. Same reading as Haiku's H2-F-6: the task does not mention airports and this is one tactic among several. A looser reading of 'similar high-demand channels' would pass gpt-6.1-sol on the hotel partners.

what_went_wrong: Court-relief rule is on the Instructions sheet only; no s3937 question states it
rationale: Instructions B9 says a departure based on ability to pay needs court-granted relief under s3937(c), but no question row mentions it. The expert's questions do not mention court relief at all (decision rule 4).

what_went_wrong: s3937 questions give the mortgage protection period only, with no contrast to other obligations
basis: carried over from C-F4 (S-C-5); expert rule 2026-11-11
rationale: The task is about mortgage accounts, and the workbook states that scope (Test Questions A1, Instructions B6). No cell mentions other obligations. The expert's questions are mortgage-only too, so neither file meets the item: E6 (decision rule 4); moved from E5 on 2026-11-11.
